title: Top Safety Tips for Mini Excavators
paragraphs: Mini excavators are some of the most useful machines on a job site — compact enough for tight spaces, but still powerful enough for digging, trenching, grading, and material handling. That same power is exactly why operator training and daily habits matter so much. The National Association of Home Builders recently published a toolbox talk on mini excavator safety, produced with the Job-Site Safety Institute, and the core guidance lines up with what we already practice on our own sites.

The basics: call 811 before any digging begins, so underground utilities are located and marked ahead of time. Once work starts, keep at least 10 feet of clearance from energized power lines, and maintain a safe distance from trench edges to avoid instability or collapse. Operators should run through the manufacturer's daily inspection checklist before startup, keep personnel clear of the swing radius, and shut the engine off before exiting the cab.
None of this is complicated, but it only works if it's consistent — every operator, every day, every site. That's the standard we hold our own crews to.
